newsitem.title: INDIA: India elects veteran Kesri to succeed Rao.
newsitem.headline: India elects veteran Kesri to succeed Rao.

text.p: India's Congress party on Monday elected veteran leader Sitaram Kesri as its provisional president to take the place of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, senior party officials said.

"Sitaram Kesri has been unanimously elected. His name was proposed by Mr. Narasimha Rao," Bhajan Lal, a senior party leader, told reporters after a meeting of the elite Congress Working Committee (CWC) which chose Rao's successor.

Rao resigned on Saturday after a court summons in a criminal conspiracy case. The "cheating" case involves a business magnate who alleges he paid $100,000 to a Rao acquaintance in 1983 in a failed attempt to win a government contract.

Kesri would be a stopgap president pending the election of a new chief by the All India Congress Committee, the powerful plenary of the party, which is expected to meet sometime next month, party officials said.
The 76-year-old Kesri is a follower of Mahatma Gandhi, independent India's spiritual father, and an active supporter of emancipation of India's low caste Hindus and minority Moslems.
The selection of a provisional chief would open the door to a fight among the many contenders for the longer-term leadership as they try to rally support.

"I have made up my mind. I don't want to go to the witness box as Congress president," the United News of India (UNI), citing party sources, quoted Rao as having said. Rao says he is innocent but resigned to help the party's image.

"Everybody proposed Kesri's name," said Oomen Deori, a CWC member. But senior leaders said Rajesh Pilot, a dissident leader who has been campaigning for a new party chief, had not immediately accepted Kesri as chief.
Rao, 75, had been under pressure to step down after leading Congress to its worst defeat in general elections ended in May.

Rao was lauded the world over for an active economic reform programme he launched in 1991. But he was seen as lacking the charisma of the Nehru-Gandhi political family, which has dominated the Congress party.
Rao succeeded former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi after Gandhi's assassination in 1991.
Kesri, party treasurer since 1979, is widely seen as a man acceptable to warring factions of the fractious party, which has ruled India for all but four years since independence from Britain in 1947.

The party has been plagued this year by a series of corruption scandals involving its senior leaders, and turned in its worst electoral performance when it was defeated in the general elections held in April and May this year.
Seven ministers resigned from Rao's cabinet early this year in a bribes-for-favours scandal. Former communications minister Sukh Ram was arrested last week in a corruption case.
The Congress party's plenary meeting is unlikely before elections in Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state, which end in early October.
"The party would not like to rock the boat before the Uttar Pradesh elections," B.G. Verghese, an analyst at the Centre for Policy Research, told Reuters.
